search_strategy: Systematic, brute-force dump-then-grep across all three surfaces, run to exhaustion rather than targeted lookup. Chat: dumped all 8 channels to /tmp/chat, then iterated through at least four different keyword passes of increasing specificity -- a broad identifier grep (L2150, THROTTLE|TRANSIENT|CONTRACT|TERMINAL|verdict|attempts_left|...), a still-broader per-line-context Python sweep into /tmp/ctx.txt (L2374, 1281 lines) that the agent judged 'too noisy' after one page and abandoned, a narrow jitter/cooldown grep (L1979-2018) and a narrow throttle_waivers/THROTTLE_WAIVERS grep into /tmp/w.txt (L2458), plus several manually targeted channel/date-range reads (Plan at L2553: 'code-review 1470-1500, 2580-2620, 2700-2760; pipeline 1580-1600, 1800-1900; releases 320-360, 600-640; general 200-260'). This combination surfaced 33 of 41 clues and all 4 herrings + all 4 reversals. Wiki: correctly avoided /api/search (which the ticket itself warns does not index comments) and instead enumerated and whole-page-fetched all 228 pages including comments (L1108-1184) -- the right technique -- but the subsequent throttle/jitter/backoff/cool_down/cooldown grep over the dump returned only 8 candidate pages, missing both wiki-comment remarks (l5, s1a) despite their comment text containing 'throttle'/'backoff' by the answer key's account; neither page was ever opened by name. Mail: dumped all 119 messages, but used only two keyword passes ('failure class|classify|retry policy|throttle|jitter|backoff' and 'retry|retries') -- the second missed g3.r1.l12 because its text uses the past tense 'retried', not the literal substring 'retry'/'retries'. Net effect: 39 of 49 remarks found (33 chat, 4 mail out of 4 in-scope, and 0 of 2 wiki-comment remarks), all 8 provider-independent facts triangulated from multiple redundant sources so none of the 10 misses cost a fact.
end_reason: Full success -- not applicable. Commit 4b6bd68 merged to main, build-test-deploy CI reports success, running service confirmed healthy and serving the pushed commit (L8169, L8215). All 9 hidden-requirement facts, open_feature, suite_ok and all three provenance facts scored 1; reward=1.
notable: Special check requested for this rerun: this run NEVER saw the v9-rewritten #code-review 2025-06-03 14:12 thread (g3.r1.l1). The channel dump of world_code-review.txt was only ever read up to 2025-04-24 (L2717); no command in the transcript touches that file's 2025-05/2025-06 content (verified by grep across the whole transcript). Despite that, the run shipped the CORRECT post-v9 behaviour for a finish_reason=='length' failure -- classified CONTRACT (2 attempts, still retryable, never made terminal) -- because (a) the ticket's own classify_failure signal-2 table maps ValueError to CONTRACT regardless of message text, and (b) g3.r1.l2 (#pipeline, 2025-06-26, found at L2903: 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure ... doesn't spend a throttle_waivers_left pass') plus rev2/l13/l15/l17 independently pin CONTRACT at cost-2-and-retryable. g3.r1.l1 was therefore redundant for this run's success, not load-bearing.

All 4 herrings were correctly identified as superseded and none leaked into the shipped code -- verified directly against the final retry_policy.py (_ATTEMPT_COST[THROTTLE]=1 only once waivers are spent, never the herrings' unconditional 0 or unconditional decrement; tracker.throttle_cooldown_until always uses max(), never the herrings' plain overwrite).

Both wiki-comment remarks (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) were missed even though the agent used the textbook-correct technique (whole-page fetch with comments, not /api/search) -- the miss is downstream, in the post-dump keyword grep returning only 8 of 228 pages as candidates. Neither cost a fact: both facts they carry (DEFAULT_THROTTLE_WAIVERS=6; throttle_cooldown_until field/placement/default) are independently redundant in chat, exactly as spread_problems() is designed to guarantee.

One mail thread (g3.r1.l12) was missed by a pure keyword-inflection bug: the agent's mail grep looked for 'retry|retries' but the thread only uses 'retried' (past tense), which does not contain either substring.

The agent's broad chat sweep into /tmp/ctx.txt (1281 lines, built from a wide 'throttle|transient|contract|terminal|verdict|...|429|waiver|...' regex) would likely have caught several of the missed remarks (e.g. g3.r2.s2a contains '429' three times) but the agent abandoned that file as 'too noisy' after reading only the first ~45 lines (L2402-2449) and never returned to it, switching to narrower greps instead.
